Subject: Tier selection and packaging question for pilot

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — team found the latency and throughputs promising. We have two immediate packaging questions as we scope the pilot: 

1) We’re trying to decide whether to run an initial pilot on the Compact (seat-based) plan with feature add-ons (real-time embeddings, private model hosting) or go straight to the Elastic throughput model (seatless, per-token). The accounting team prefers a predictable monthly seat cost but the product group wants headroom for bursty traffic.

2) What does mid-quarter upgrading/downgrading look like? Specifically: proration, SKU swaps for private model hosting, and whether we can apply a short pilot discount that can be reconciled at renewal.

Attached is a short spreadsheet with our expected usage profile for September–November. Can you sketch two packaged options and an expected first‑quarter cost range? Also share any standard concession ranges you typically offer for first pilots.

Goal: decide by next Tuesday so procurement can start the PO.

Thanks,
Maria Gomez
Head of Product
BrightWave Health

Attachment: brightwave_pricing_request.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet stub)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria@brightwavehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T17:32:00Z
Subject: Re: Tier selection and packaging question for pilot

Hi Maria —

Really helpful context and thanks for the spreadsheet. Quick sketch below — happy to walk through live tomorrow.

Option A — Compact (seat-based) + feature add-ons - Structure: 10 seats, fixed monthly seat fee + optional add-on SKUs for realtime embeddings and private model hosting - Pros: predictable monthly cost, simpler procurement (PO for seats), clear feature gating - Cons: may require temporary surge capacity or temporary burst credits for peak days - Pricing note: pilot concession we typically offer is 10–15% off list for a 3‑month pilot with a 6– or 12‑month renewal commitment.

Option B — Elastic throughput (seatless, per-token) with soft commit - Structure: baseline throughput commitment (tokens/min) + overage per token; private model hosting treated as an add-on SKU (flat monthly + per-hour training/ingest fee) - Pros: handles bursty traffic without seat churn, lower friction for scaling up during pilot - Cons: less predictable spend unless you purchase a higher baseline commit - Pricing note: we can do a smaller pilot commit with a 12% effective pilot discount for the first quarter and cap overage at an agreed rate.

On mid-quarter changes:
- Upgrades: we can do pro‑rated upgrades immediately (no prorate fee) — customer is billed the pro rata difference for remainder of billing period.
- Downgrades: standard policy is next-billing-cycle effective (no immediate credit); we can entertain a one-time credit only for enterprise deals with finance approval.

I’ve attached a quick calculator showing the two scenarios against the numbers you sent. If you like, we can:
1) Schedule a 30-minute call Wed morning to run numbers live;
2) Draft a short amendment that captures the pilot concession and temporary commitment;
3) Create a mutual action plan (MAP) so procurement has next steps.

Proposed pilot concession (prelim): 15% off list for a 3‑month pilot if BrightWave commits to a 6‑month renewal or provides a $Xk minimum spend (we can flex that). If you want a firmer discount, I’ll loop in RevOps for approval.

Attachment: redwood_pilot_discount_calc.pdf (pricing calc stub)

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the context — quick take: 

- Discount: RevOps should be able to approve a 12% pilot discount for 3 months without exec sign‑off. 15% is borderline and usually needs RevOps signoff + justification (pipeline motion / reference ability).
- Proration: OK to waive proration fees for upgrades during pilot (good for conversion signal). Downgrades should be next-cycle effective; don’t promise credits.
- Private model hosting: $2k/mo base + $150/hr ingest/training is reasonable as an add-on SKU. Include a data transfer estimate as a separate line item.

If they want 15% exactly, I’ll reach out to RevOps and request a one-off concession with a short business justification. Recommend we prepare a 1‑page amendment template for pilot discounts to speed legal review.

— Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
